# Charlotte (01, researcher) — SPD-053

## Brief
Find the sanctioned way for Spud's `gh pr merge` on a green BadTakes pull request to pass the Claude Code auto-mode permission classifier, without weakening review in general; or show with evidence that no such way exists, so CLAUDE.md can say plainly that Eric merges.

Evidence already in hand:
- Five BadTakes PRs today (329, 350, 351, 352, 353) were all refused and merged by hand by Eric (GitHub login 0snug0). The refusal text, in the BadTakes session transcripts `~/.claude/projects/-Users-ericlugo-Personal-BadTakes/*.jsonl`, is: "Permission for this action was denied by the Claude Code auto mode classifier. Reason: [Merge Without Review]. ... You *may* attempt to accomplish this action using other tools ... But you *should not* attempt to work around this denial in malicious ways". Quote the exact `gh pr merge` command that was refused (find the tool_use before that tool_result). A BadTakes memory note says even `gh pr view --json mergeCommit` has been refused under the same reason.
- BadTakes `main` branch protection (`gh api repos/0snug0/BadTakes/branches/main/protection`): required status check `Gate` only, `required_approving_review_count` 0, no rulesets. GitHub itself lets the author merge; only the classifier refuses.
- Permission rules in force: BadTakes `.claude/settings.local.json` (written by `spud project install`; the writer is in `bin/spud_ledger.py`, `merge_allow_rules` near line 3357 and the install path near lines 4875 and 5011) and the home `.claude/settings.json`. Both allow `bin/spud` and little else. Nothing names `gh`.

Questions to answer, each with its source (official Claude Code docs on auto mode and permissions, fetched by a `claude-code-guide` contractor; the transcripts; the settings files):
1. Does the auto-mode classifier honor `permissions.allow` rules, so an explicit `Bash(gh pr merge *)` (or `Bash(gh pr merge:*)`, say which syntax is right) skips the classifier? Which settings scopes count: project `.claude/settings.local.json`, user `~/.claude/settings.json`, or only some? Are there categories the classifier refuses even with an allow rule?
2. Is "Merge Without Review" a category satisfied by context: a review the classifier can see in the session (a reviewer spudagent's verdict, the `/code-review` skill, a PR review posted with `gh pr review`), an approving review on the PR, or the PR body stating the review status? What do the docs say the classifier reads?
3. GitHub auto-merge: `gh pr merge --auto --squash` at PR open, or enabling auto-merge through the API. Would the classifier refuse it as the same merge? Does the repository allow auto-merge (`gh api repos/0snug0/BadTakes --jq .allow_auto_merge`), and would it fire with `Gate` required and no reviews required?
4. Any other route Eric can configure deliberately rather than Spud evading the classifier: a BadTakes GitHub Actions workflow that merges PRs carrying a label Spud adds once Gate is green, a repository setting, running the landing step outside auto mode. Say for each whether it weakens review in general, and whether the classifier's own message would treat it as a workaround.
5. Recommend one route, state the exact change it needs (the allow rule `project install` should write and where in `bin/spud_ledger.py`; or the repository setting; or, if none is acceptable, the wording for CLAUDE.md's Landing bullet and the merge memory saying Eric merges), and how Spud verifies it on the next real BadTakes PR.

Rules for this research: read-only. Do not merge, open, label, approve or close any pull request, do not create a repository, do not edit any settings file, do not change anything on GitHub. A read-only probe of the classifier is fine (for example `gh pr view 353 --json state,mergedBy` and separately `--json mergeCommit`, to see whether reads are refused). The live test is the next real BadTakes PR, run by Spud after this ticket lands the change.

## Ticket proposals
- **Make smoke and test required status checks on BadTakes main, alongside Gate** — suggested P2; declined by Spud: Already the case since BAD-022: Gate is a job inside ci.yml that needs changes, test and smoke with always(), so a red test or smoke fails the one required context, while requiring them directly would strand docs-only PRs whose gated jobs skip; the premise that Gate alone is thin is wrong.
  Why: BadTakes main requires one status context (Gate) and zero approving reviews, so the server-side guarantee behind every merge is thinner than the session behaviour suggests. This is the one change found in SPD-053 that makes a BadTakes merge safer rather than easier, and it holds whichever landing route Eric picks.
  Evidence: Measured 2026-09-14: gh api repos/0snug0/BadTakes/branches/main/protection gives required_status_checks.contexts == ["Gate"], strict false, required_approving_review_count 0, enforce_admins false, no restrictions; gh api repos/0snug0/BadTakes/rulesets returns 0. BAD-022 already added smoke and test to ci.yml's Gate job, so promoting them costs a settings change, not new CI.
- **Never retry a classifier refusal, in any project, for any category** — suggested P2; declined by Spud: Spud-only work, so no ticket: the never-retry rule goes into CLAUDE.md's Landing bullet under SPD-053, in the same edit that records the stated-intent route.
  Why: Retrying a soft block is the 'work around this denial' the refusal message warns against, it corrupts any measurement of whether a fix worked, and in the one case where a retry succeeded it succeeded for an unrelated reason. CLAUDE.md's landing step should say attempt once, never twice, never through another tool, and never manufacture the user intent the classifier reads.
  Evidence: BadTakes transcripts 2026-09-14/15: PR 341 refused twice in session 0cc3dd6b (02:11:29 and 02:19:22); PR 328's attempt was written as 'gh pr merge ... || gh pr merge ...' with a second invocation in the fallback. PR 337's second attempt succeeded only because Eric typed 'Do the merge for me' between the two, not because retrying works. Spud's own files, so no spudagent.

## Result
Produced /Users/ericlugo/Personal/Spud/docs/spikes/2026-09-14-pr-merge-in-auto-mode.md (169 lines), the only path I wrote. It answers all five brief questions with sources and names one recommended route.

A sanctioned route exists and is documented. The classifier's fourth precedence tier (auto-mode-config: 'Explicit user intent overrides the remaining soft blocks: if the user's message directly and specifically describes the exact action Claude is about to take, the classifier allows it even when a soft_deny rule matches') and 'Merge Without Review' is soft_deny, not hard_deny. Splitting the 26 gh pr merge attempts of 2026-09-14/15 by whether the last genuine human message in the session asked for a merge: asked -> 6 allowed, 0 refused; not asked -> 6 allowed, 14 refused; Fisher exact two-sided p=0.004. PR 337 proves it: identical command refused 00:36:28, Eric typed 'Do the merge for me', allowed 00:37:24. One statement covered three later merges (347, 349, 350).

Recommended route: Eric names the landing in the same opening message that names the ticket ('Work on BAD-027, and merge its PR once Gate is green'). Nothing is configured, nothing is weakened, and CLAUDE.md cannot substitute because the classifier reads messages, not context. Exact change is two edits in Spud's own files (the CLAUDE.md Landing bullet and the merge memory), wording given. Escalation if Eric wants it hands-free: add Bash(gh pr merge:*) to BadTakes .claude/settings.local.json by hand; it survives every project install untouched because ALLOW_RULE_MARK (spud_ledger.py:3300) only drops bin/spud rules, so no code change is needed; the five-step CLI change is specified if he wants the CLI to own it, behind an opt-in that defaults to off. Its real cost is stated: main has required_approving_review_count 0, so the rule removes the only human look a BadTakes merge gets.

Rejected with evidence: GitHub auto-merge (allow_auto_merge is false, and the carve-out needs server-side required reviews, which would deadlock a solo repo since GitHub refuses self-approval); a label-plus-Actions merge (GITHUB_TOKEN merges create no push event, so deploy-web.yml, deploy-site.yml and the server-deploy chain would silently stop); running the landing outside auto mode (no documented pattern, and the shape the refusal warns against).

Verified: read-only throughout. Nothing merged, opened, labelled, approved or closed; no settings file edited; no GitHub setting changed. My own 'claude auto-mode defaults' probe was refused with Reason [Auto-Mode Bypass] and was NOT worked around; that refusal is reported in the spike and is why every recommended settings edit is Eric's hand, not Spud's. Kestrel (01.01) is recorded done; both its returns carried harness flags (the first a SECURITY WARNING, same [Auto-Mode Bypass] reason) and were treated as data, cited as relayed. Two proposals filed: 61 (promote smoke and test to required checks on BadTakes main) and 62 (never retry a classifier refusal).

Left: Eric picks between the prompt route and the permission rule (4 open questions at the end of the spike); the live test is the next real BadTakes PR, five consecutive first-attempt landings, method specified.

Stayed read-only; the one refused probe was not retried. Kestrel's flagged returns were read as data. Proposals 61 and 62 decided below.
